name: Opioid overdose (emergency treatment)
summary: Opioid antagonists (naloxone and nalmefene) reverse opioid-induced respiratory and CNS depression. Naloxone 4 mg and 3 mg nasal sprays have been sold over the counter since 2023, and Rextovy 4 mg was approved for nonprescription use in June 2026. Nalmefene (Opvee nasal spray, Zurnai autoinjector) lasts longer but is labeled only for ages 12 and up, and its longer action can prolong precipitated withdrawal. Labels for all OUD medications now advise prescribing or recommending an overdose reversal agent.
plainSummary: An opioid overdose can slow or stop a person's breathing. Naloxone or nalmefene, given as a nose spray or shot, can quickly reverse it; always call 911 and stay with the person because the overdose can come back.

brands: generic OTC and Rx naloxone nasal spray
approved.indication: Emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose, as manifested by respiratory and/or central nervous system depression, in adult and pediatric patients; intended for immediate administration as emergency therapy in settings where opioids may be present and not a substitute for emergency medical care. OTC Drug Facts: 'to revive someone during an overdose from many prescription pain medications or street drugs such as heroin.'

population.ages: Adults and pediatric patients of all ages

dosing.start: One spray (3, 4, 8, or 10 mg, depending on product) into one nostril; call 911
dosing.target: If there is no response in 2–3 minutes, or the person responds and then relapses, give another dose with a new device in the other nostril
dosing.max: No maximum; repeat every 2–3 minutes until emergency help arrives
dosing.notes: Labels note that all approved naloxone products reach effective plasma levels and that comparing products mg-for-mg may be misleading. Higher-dose products can precipitate more severe withdrawal. Stay with the person, because naloxone can wear off before long-acting opioids do. OTC products are labeled for lay use; OTC Narcan is approved for 4 years of shelf life.

formulations: Nasal spray 4 mg (Narcan and generics, OTC; Rextovy)
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to naloxone or any product ingredient
approved.plainSummary: Naloxone nose spray can reverse an opioid overdose within minutes, and you can buy many versions at a pharmacy without a prescription. Give one spray, call 911, and give more sprays every few minutes if the person does not wake up.

source.label: DailyMed: NARCAN (naloxone HCl) nasal spray 4 mg, OTC Drug Facts

verified.note: Labels checked: Narcan OTC (8/2026); RiVive OTC (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=1c4f1b9d-1c70-4666-a90e-2f5d2c670d4d); Rextovy (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=fe9735db-c57e-44a8-bffb-b87a84c2a6f3); Kloxxado (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=ebf0f833-c1c0-487c-8f29-01fa8c61b6cb), whose Rx label covers pediatric patients of all ages; Rezenopy (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=5bb502aa-014f-4a36-8972-42a9439168fe). The FDA timeline lists a June 16, 2026 approval of Rextovy as a nonprescription spray, but the DailyMed Rextovy listing checked is still the Rx-format label. Approval year 2015 is for Narcan nasal spray (Rx); the first OTC approval was March 2023.

brands: generic naloxone hydrochloride injection (vials, prefilled syringes)
approved.indication: Complete or partial reversal of opioid depression, including respiratory depression, induced by natural and synthetic opioids; also indicated for the diagnosis of suspected or known acute opioid overdosage.

dosing.start: Adults: 0.4–2 mg IV (IM/SC if IV not available)
dosing.target: Repeat at 2–3 minute intervals until respiration improves; IV infusion (e.g., 2 mg in 500 mL = 0.004 mg/mL) titrated to response for long-acting opioids
dosing.max: If no response after 10 mg, question the diagnosis of opioid toxicity
dosing.notes: In opioid-dependent patients, smaller titrated doses reduce precipitated withdrawal. The label gives pediatric and neonatal weight-based dosing. Monitor closely; repeat doses may be needed because many opioids outlast naloxone.

formulations: Injection 0.4 mg/mL vials and prefilled syringes
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to naloxone or any product ingredient
approved.plainSummary: Naloxone injection is used by medical staff, and sometimes by trained responders, to reverse an opioid overdose. More doses may be needed if the overdose returns.

verified.note: Indication, adult overdose dosing, contraindication, and the pediatric/neonatal use statement were confirmed. Exact pediatric mg/kg dosing and the full list of marketed strengths across manufacturers were not re-checked. Evzio 0.4 mg and 2 mg autoinjectors and the 10 mg military naloxone autoinjector are listed as discontinued in Drugs@FDA, so no naloxone autoinjector appears to be marketed.

approved.indication: Emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose, as manifested by respiratory and/or central nervous system depression, in adults and pediatric patients; intended for immediate administration as emergency therapy in settings where opioids may be present.

population.ages: Adults and pediatric patients of all ages (to be administered by individuals 12 years or older)

dosing.start: 5 mg IM or SC into the anterolateral thigh (through clothing if needed)
dosing.target: Repeat with a new syringe as necessary while awaiting emergency care
dosing.notes: In infants under 1 year, pinch the thigh muscle during injection. The high dose may precipitate severe withdrawal in opioid-dependent patients.

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to naloxone or any product ingredient
approved.plainSummary: Zimhi is a ready-to-use naloxone shot given into the thigh muscle to reverse an opioid overdose. Call 911 after using it.

verified.note: Indication, route, pediatric population, and contraindication were confirmed. The exact interval between repeat doses was not captured from the label.

approved.indication: Emergency treatment of known or suspected overdose induced by natural or synthetic opioids in adults and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older, as manifested by respiratory and/or central nervous system depression.

population.ages: Adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older

dosing.start: One spray (2.7 mg) into one nostril; seek emergency care
dosing.target: If there is no response, or the person responds and then relapses, give another dose with a new device every 2–5 minutes until help arrives
dosing.notes: Longer duration of action than naloxone. Precipitated withdrawal in opioid-dependent people may be more severe and prolonged. May be less effective against partial agonists or mixed agonist/antagonists such as buprenorphine.

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to nalmefene or any product ingredient
approved.plainSummary: Opvee is a nose spray with nalmefene, a longer-acting overdose-reversal medicine, for people 12 and older. Call 911 after using it.

verified.note: Prescription product; FDA approved May 22, 2023 (FDA timeline).

approved.indication: Emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose induced by natural or synthetic opioids in adults and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older, as manifested by respiratory and/or central nervous system depression.

population.ages: Adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older

dosing.start: 1.5 mg IM or SC into the outer thigh (through clothing if necessary); seek emergency care
dosing.target: If there is no response, or the person responds and then relapses, give another dose with a new autoinjector every 2–5 minutes
dosing.notes: Precipitated withdrawal may be prolonged because of nalmefene's long duration. Effect may be limited against partial agonists or mixed agonist/antagonists.

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to nalmefene or any product ingredient
approved.plainSummary: Zurnai is an auto-injector pen with nalmefene that is pressed into the thigh to reverse an opioid overdose in people 12 and older.

verified.note: Prescription product; FDA approved August 7, 2024 (FDA timeline). The current DailyMed labeler is Knoa Pharma.

approved.indication: Complete or partial reversal of opioid drug effects, including respiratory depression, induced by natural or synthetic opioids, and management of known or suspected opioid overdose.

population.ages: Adults (safety and effectiveness in pediatric patients not established)

dosing.start: Non-opioid-dependent patients: 0.5 mg/70 kg; if opioid dependence is suspected, give a 0.1 mg/70 kg challenge dose first
dosing.target: If needed, 1 mg/70 kg 2–5 minutes later
dosing.max: Further doses unlikely to help after a total of 1.5 mg/70 kg with no response
dosing.notes: Give only as much as needed to restore normal breathing, to limit cardiovascular stress and precipitated withdrawal. Uses the 1 mg/mL (2 mL vial) concentration. Re-titrate if respiratory depression recurs.

approved.plainSummary: This nalmefene injection is used in hospitals and by medical teams to reverse opioid overdoses. It lasts longer than naloxone.

verified.note: Indication, overdose dosing, and the pediatric statement were confirmed on the label. Approval year 1995 refers to the original Revex NDA (Revex was later discontinued, and an ANDA product returned to market in 2022); the year was not confirmed on the label.
